class.name: CheckButton
class.brief_description: A button that represents a binary choice.
class.description: [CheckButton] is a toggle button displayed as a check field. It's similar to [CheckBox] in functionality, but it has a different appearance. To follow established UX patterns, it's recommended to use [CheckButton] when toggling it has an [b]immediate[/b] effect on something. For example, it can be used when pressing it shows or hides advanced settings, without asking the user to confirm this action. See also [BaseButton] which contains common properties and methods associated with this node.

theme_items.theme_item: The color of the checked icon when the checkbox is pressed.
The color of the unchecked icon when the checkbox is not pressed.
The vertical offset used when rendering the toggle icons (in pixels).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is checked (for left-to-right layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is checked and disabled (for left-to-right layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is checked and disabled (for right-to-left layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is checked (for right-to-left layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is unchecked (for left-to-right layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is unchecked and disabled (for left-to-right layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is unchecked and disabled (for right-to-left layouts).
The icon to display when the [CheckButton] is unchecked (for right-to-left layouts).

The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is checked. If one of the switch style boxes isn't a [StyleBoxEmpty], the switch is drawn with them instead of the icons, and changes between the states with the style transitions. It then has the largest minimum size of these style boxes in every state, and a [StyleBoxEmpty] draws nothing. [theme_item button_checked_color] and [theme_item button_unchecked_color] don't tint them, set the colors in the style boxes instead.
The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is checked and disabled, see [theme_item checked]. If it's a [StyleBoxEmpty], [theme_item checked] is used instead.

The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is checked and disabled, in right-to-left layouts, see [theme_item checked]. If it's a [StyleBoxEmpty], [theme_item checked_mirrored] is used instead, then [theme_item checked_disabled] and [theme_item checked].
The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is checked, in right-to-left layouts, see [theme_item checked]. If it's a [StyleBoxEmpty], [theme_item checked] is used instead.

The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is unchecked. If one of the switch style boxes isn't a [StyleBoxEmpty], the switch is drawn with them instead of the icons, and changes between the states with the style transitions. It then has the largest minimum size of these style boxes in every state, and a [StyleBoxEmpty] draws nothing. [theme_item button_checked_color] and [theme_item button_unchecked_color] don't tint them, set the colors in the style boxes instead.
The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is unchecked and disabled, see [theme_item unchecked]. If it's a [StyleBoxEmpty], [theme_item unchecked] is used instead.

The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is unchecked and disabled, in right-to-left layouts, see [theme_item unchecked]. If it's a [StyleBoxEmpty], [theme_item unchecked_mirrored] is used instead, then [theme_item unchecked_disabled] and [theme_item unchecked].
The style box of the switch when the [CheckButton] is unchecked, in right-to-left layouts, see [theme_item unchecked]. If it's a [StyleBoxEmpty], [theme_item unchecked] is used instead.
